name: Deep Hyssop Violet
lede: Deep Hyssop Violet is a muted, lighter cousin of Dark Hyssop Violet, both named for the herb and both recorded by Ridgway in 1912 and classed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955.

sections.title: A lighter hyssop
sections.body:
Deep Hyssop Violet shares its root with [[dark-hyssop-violet|Dark Hyssop Violet]]: both trace to hyssop, the aromatic herb, in our data [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas plots this lighter member on the same plate, XXXVI, at hue 59′′, tone i, one step up from its darker sibling's tone k, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files it as block 223, a neighbor of that sibling's block 224 [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 46, chroma 20, hue 316 degrees, noticeably lighter than Dark Hyssop Violet's lightness of 39 [1].

Its nearest distinct neighbor by computed color distance is [[purplish-grey|Purplish Grey]], 2.6 units away and read in our data as "almost the same" [2]. [[aster|Aster]] sits almost as close, 2.9 units off, also "almost the same" [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a close match covers enough of the canvas in only 9, as photographed, rarer than 69 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in paintings from the 1800s, at 1.7 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive [3]. Its earliest archive match is a painting from 1842 by the Danish painter Kølle, and its latest is from 1915, a narrow 73-year window compared to the centuries-long spans of some other colors in this family [3].
